extracted.name: Pan-Fried Bao Zi
extracted.description: Now, making baozi has become a special tradition in our home, just like it was for my grandparents. It takes practice, but once you get the hang of it, it’s really fun! I love that my daughter is just as excited about baozi as I was growing up.
instruction_lines: Make the Dough: In a bowl, mix the flour, salt, yeast, and warm water. Knead into a smooth dough, then cover it and let it rise until it doubles in size (about 1 hour).
Prepare the Filling: In a food processor, combine ground beef, onion, scallions, salt, pepper, five-spice powder, soy sauces, oyster sauce, and sesame oil. Blend until well mixed and set aside.

Shape the Dough: After the dough has risen, punch it down to release air bubbles. Roll it out into a log and cut it into 21 pieces (around 35 g each). Roll each piece into a thick wrapper, leaving a slight bump in the middle.
Fill and Seal: Add a spoonful of the filling to the center of each wrapper. Pinch the edges together to seal, forming the bao zi.
Rest the Bao Zi Let the filled bao zi rest for about 15 minutes before cooking.
Fry the Bao Zi: Heat some oil in a cast-iron pan over medium heat. Place the bao zi in the pan, flat side down, and fry for 2-3 minutes until golden brown on the bottom.
Simmer: Pour the flour and water mixture around the bao zi (not directly on top), cover the pan with a lid, and let it simmer for about 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Crisp the Bottom: Drizzle a bit more oil around the bao zi and cook until the bottom is thick and golden brown.
Garnish and Serve: Sprinkle black sesame seeds and chopped scallions over the fried bao zi before serving. Enjoy!
